newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAL mulls shifting some domestic flights to unit.
newsitem.headline: JAL mulls shifting some domestic flights to unit.

text.p: Japan Airlines Co Ltd (JAL) said on Friday that it was considering transferring part of its domestic flight operations to a subsidiary to reduce costs.

JAL, which is Japan's largest airline company, may transfer the operation of 11 of its domestic flights to Japan Transocean Air Co Ltd, in which JAL holds a 51 percent stake, or it may create a new subsidiary for this, a JAL spokesman said.
The company has not yet decided on any concrete plan, but it is considering various possibilities for improving the efficiency of its operations, the spokesman said.
JAL is considering transferring operations for flights between Osaka and several locations in Kyushu in southern Japan, as well as between Osaka and two cities in northern Japan.
